text: Lecture slides use a dark blue title bar with white text.
Put no more than one worked example on a slide.
Slide font is never smaller than 24 point.
Start each lecture with a two-minute recap of the previous class.
End lecture five minutes early on the day before an exam.
Use the document camera for worked examples, not the whiteboard.
Slide decks are named by lecture number, like L14.
Include a real-world photo on the first slide of each new chapter.
Never use animations or transitions in slides.
Number every slide in the bottom right corner.
Use a clicker question roughly every fifteen minutes in lecture.
Write the lecture outline as three bullet points on the board before class.
Use blue and black markers only; red is hard to see from the back.
Leave the classroom door open until five minutes after the start.
Play no music before class.
Take a one-minute stretch break at the halfway point of a 75-minute class.
Wear the lapel microphone in the large lecture hall.
Bring a spare HDMI adapter to every class.
Use Desmos for in-class graph demonstrations.
Show the day's agenda on the first slide.
Department travel requests go in at least six weeks ahead.
Annual review materials go to the associate head each winter.
Committee meeting notes are filed in the shared drive under the year.
Reimbursement receipts are scanned the same day.
Conference abstracts are drafted in plain text first.
Seminar speakers get a thank-you note within a week.
Letters of recommendation need at least two weeks' notice.
A recommendation letter is at most one page.
Advising appointments are thirty minutes.
Peer teaching observations are written up within three days.
Course evaluation comments are read only after grades are posted.
Office supply orders go through the department's front desk.
Use the department letterhead template for formal letters.
Keep the assistant drawer docked on the right.
Keep the office door open during office hours.
Keep the desk whiteboard for the week's three priorities.
Check the department mailbox on Mondays.
Keep spare pencils for bubble sheets in the top drawer.
Park in Lot 51 on exam nights.
Bring the laptop charger on lecture days.
Keep a printed class list in the bag for fire drills.
Lock the filing cabinet with old exams every evening.
Shred graded papers older than one year each May.
Keep a first-aid kit in the office.
The pub-quiz team for the department social needs four people.
Email the department head, not the dean, about room problems.
Announce seminar talks on the department listserv, not Canvas.
The faculty meeting agenda is announced a week ahead.
Quiz bowl volunteers from the math club get a pizza lunch.
Key requests for the tutoring room go to the building proctor.
The copy room key is on the blue lanyard.
A rubric for peer teaching observations is on the department site.
Curve fitting examples in my research talks use the cereal-box dataset.
Version control for my research code is on the department GitLab.
The calculus placement exam is run by the advising office.

Sign reimbursement forms in blue ink.
Address envelopes for recommendation letters by hand.
Subject GRE advising questions go to the graduate office.
Table tents with names are used at the department retreat.
Dates for the colloquium series come from the seminar chair.
The department coordinator handles room keys.
Extra chairs for the review room are in closet 204.
The partial differential equations reading group meets in the library.
Research group students present once a semester.
Referee reports are written within three weeks of the request.
Thesis committee forms are signed electronically.
Outreach visits to high schools are limited to two per term.
